title: Startup brief recovery survives transient database outages and stops on shutdown
steps: Run brief-build startup recovery cases against PostgreSQL. Inject ENOTFOUND during its first read, SQLSTATE 53100 during its settlement write, and ECONNRESET for an uncertain applying row. Also exercise a permanent SQL error, transient retry exhaustion and shutdown during backoff.
expect: Transient startup failures settle orphaned rows without a customer poll and retain LOST_ON_RESTART and lostFrom metadata.
An uncertain applying row retains LOST_PLACING and cannot silently become safe to replay.
Permanent errors stop after one query; transient failures stop at the configured attempt budget with a terminal log.
Shutdown cancels the backoff before another query or row write. Existing live heartbeat protection still passes.
fence: Bounded transient retry of recoverLost with observed updated_at fencing and cancellable recovery waits

cmd: --test-name-pattern=startup recovery|a row too fresh to judge at start
tests: startup recovery retries a transient database failure without a customer poll
startup recovery stops on permanent errors and after its transient retry budget
shutdown cancels startup recovery backoff before it can write an orphaned row
a row too fresh to judge at start is settled once it misses its heartbeat, and a beating one is left alone
